benefits: Valid for your whole degree, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility requirements
Applied prior to the census date of each trimester on meeting the ongoing enrolment requirements
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand.
Be a new, commencing student who has received an offer to study by the scholarship application closing date.
Have a minimum GPA in previous studies of 6.0 or above on a 7 point scale or equivalent.
Satisfy all academic and English language entry requirements for your chosen undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program.
Be a full-time student starting in 2026 or 2027.
requirements: Be a commencing student in the trimester you are applying for, and apply by the closing date for that trimester.
Hold International Fee Paying student status; any change from that status makes the scholarship no longer available.
Enrol full-time, make progress in studies, meet the requirements of the program of study and meet student visa requirements.

Pass all courses each trimester and progress to enrol in the next; a minimum cumulative GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 point grading scale must be maintained annually to qualify for the following year tuition fee deductions.
Remain enrolled in the program stated on the Letter of Offer issued by Griffith International Admissions; deferral of the scholarship is not permitted.

Scholarship applies to undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees only, excluding Higher Degree Research, online programs, non-award, Study Abroad Program, Diploma programs, Masters Qualifying Program, MBA (program code 5158), Griffith English Language Institute programs, programs offered only part time, and programs delivered onshore or offshore in collaboration with a partner organisation.

Griffith ID and program of study entered in the application form
Intended start trimester (Trimester 3 2026, Trimester 1 2027 or Trimester 2 2027)

Strong academic merit, with a minimum GPA of 6.0 or above on a 7 point scale or equivalent

Competitive selection with limited scholarship numbers; once the acceptance limit is reached, the Griffith International Scholarship Office advises applicants that all available scholarships have been awarded
Recipients are expected to be profiled in marketing activities for Griffith University
coverage: The scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees only for the duration of the program, on meeting the ongoing enrolment requirements.
Scholarship applies to undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees only.
Living costs, accommodation and travel are not covered; the student must pay the remaining balance of fees based on their enrolment by census date.
application_method: Apply to study an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program at Griffith University.
Once you have your Letter of Offer, apply for the scholarship by the closing date for your commencing trimester, including academic records and a personal statement.
If you meet all the eligibility requirements, a University panel will review your application.
Griffith will advise the outcome of your application by the published date (e.g. 11 December 2026 for Trimester 1 2027).
Accept both the program offer and the scholarship by the deadline in the Scholarship Letter, or the scholarship is withdrawn.
official.application_route: Apply online for a Griffith undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program, then after receiving a conditional or unconditional Letter of Offer submit the Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship application form (5-10 minutes) with certified academic records and a 250-500 word personal statement.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand; no residency rule published
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students only - Australian and New Zealand citizens are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Available for undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs only; excludes Higher Degree Research, online programs, non-award study, Study Abroad Program, Diploma programs, Masters Qualifying Program, MBA (program code 5158), Griffith English Language Institute programs, part-time-only programs and programs delivered onshore or offshore in collaboration with a partner organisation
official.duration: Valid for your whole degree, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility requirements; course duration is defined as the Program Length of the first degree program stated in the Letter of Offer, less any credit received for previous study
official.description: Griffith University states that its Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship "rewards a number of exceptional international students commencing in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework degree programs at Griffith University each year", with an award value of 50% of tuition fees valid for the whole degree, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility requirements.
official.english_requirement: Scholarship applicants must satisfy the academic and English language entry requirements of their chosen program. Griffith's published standard entry tests for undergraduate, postgraduate and research programs: IELTS (Academic) minimum 6.5 with no subscore less than 6.0; TOEFL iBT and Paper Edition score of 79 with no sub-score less than 19; Pearson Test of English (Academic) overall 55 with no score less than 47; ISLPR no score less than 3+ in each skill; Michigan English Test 55 overall with no score less than 47. Applicants whose previous study was undertaken in English may be exempt, assessed as part of the application. Some degrees require higher levels of English or only accept specific tests.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a half-tuition waiver, not a living scholarship: Griffith takes 50% off your coursework tuition before each trimester's census date, so the money you actually save depends entirely on the program you pick and is never paid as a lump sum. You cannot apply until you hold a conditional or unconditional offer, which means the scholarship application comes second and still has to land before your intake's closing date. Budget the remaining half of tuition plus flights, insurance, accommodation and living costs yourself, because none of that is funded. Check your program code first, because research degrees, online study and the MBA (5158) are all excluded from this award.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international applicants with a 6.0+ GPA on a 7-point scale who already hold a Griffith coursework offer and can self-fund the other half of the fees and all living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a conditional or unconditional Griffith offer first - the scholarship form cannot be submitted without it.
Have academic certificates and transcripts certified or attested as true copies before you upload; plain scans are not enough.
Write the personal statement to the published brief (why you are applying, your chosen Griffith program, how you will use your degree to make an impact) and keep it inside 250-500 words.

Confirm your program is not on the exclusion list - research degrees, online, non-award, Study Abroad, Diploma, Masters Qualifying, MBA 5158, GELI English, part-time-only or partner-delivered - and that you will study full-time.
Diary the closing date for your exact intake (28 November 2026 for Trimester 1 2027; 2 January 2027 for Australian Year 12; 10 April 2027 for Trimester 2 2027) and work backwards from it.
Check your English test is valid for two years and meets your specific degree's requirement, which can be higher than the standard 6.5.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a conditional or unconditional offer, or missing the closing date for the specific commencing trimester.
A personal statement that ignores the published prompt or falls outside the 250-500 word range.
Choosing an excluded program such as the MBA (5158), a research degree, online study, a Diploma, Masters Qualifying or a partner-delivered program.
Failing to accept the scholarship by the date in the Scholarship Letter, which causes it to be withdrawn.
Dropping below full-time enrolment or failing courses, which ends eligibility for the tuition deductions.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of coursework tuition fees payable by each census date, plus all living costs, accommodation, overseas student health cover, flights and visa costs - none of which the scholarship covers.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts must be certified or attested true copies, not unverified scans or photographs.
The form asks for your Griffith ID, so you must already exist in Griffith's admissions system before you can apply.
The personal statement has a hard 250-500 word window and a specific prompt, so treat it like a marked question rather than a general motivation letter.
Up to three qualifications can be listed, but every completed study listed needs its own certified copy attached.
English results must be under two years old and meet the requirement of your specific degree, not just the university minimum.
alerts: Scholarship numbers are limited - once the acceptance cap is reached Griffith withdraws the remaining scholarships, so applying on the last day is risky.
Deferral is not permitted, so a delayed start means giving the award up entirely.
You must stay in the exact program named on your Letter of Offer; changing programs forfeits the scholarship.
A cumulative GPA of 5.5 on the 7.0 scale must be maintained to unlock the following year's deductions, reviewed at the end of Trimester 2 for T1 starters and end of Trimester 1 for T2/T3 starters.
If you withdraw or cancel your studies, the scholarship amount already applied is non-refundable.
Australian and New Zealand citizens are excluded, and there is no residency alternative published for them.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for the coursework program, wait for the Letter of Offer, then complete the short online Vice Chancellor's scholarship form (5-10 minutes) attaching certified academic records and the 250-500 word statement; a University panel reviews it and the outcome is released by the published date.
